txt: As the hum grows louder, modulating, but always unnaturally, uncomfortably low, like it's coming not from the speakers, but also from inside your chest. Breathing is becoming difficult...
He doesn't quite catch your meaning. "Oh... sure." He tries to mimic your rotational action but just ends up shrugging.
He drums his fingers on the counter. "I doubt the real Man from Hjelmdall was as poor a role model as the one in the popular literature."

He dusts off a case, then takes out the tape and places it on the tape player. "This recording comes from down the coast... Wasn't looking to record anything specific -- just left a recording device there one morning."
He frowns. "Aphotic paths? Counter-radiance networks? Antimagnetism? It's darkness. That's all I know. Sell me something *lighter*."
He frowns. "But... why?"
He frowns. "Pyrholidon is just something I... you know, since the People's Pile disaster." He coughs, as if to mark his words.
He grimaces. "I wouldn't go so far as to say that I'm a fan. But I do think the Hjelmdallermann Saga is an integral part of our shared reality."
He gulps. "That's... not enough."
He hands you the cardboard and you notice there's something written on it. "Stick this to the light and people will know that it's *yours*."
He hands you the sign then watches you attach it to the street light using the sticky tack he put on the back. "There you go. Beautiful job."
He hesitates. "I was... I was with the Emergency Relief Brigade. You know, after the People's Pile disaster." He coughs, as if to mark his words.
He hesitates. "There's a reason why everyone's tried to forget any of it ever happened, and why no one has tried to repair or replace the Pile."
He inclines his head. "You should."
He knits his eyebrows, thinking, then says, "Alright, let's see it."
He lets out a long sigh. "I'm in debt, officer. I've felt *stuck* for a long time." He looks at the paper in your hand. "Those stocks -- they could be my way out."
He looks at the bronze-coloured bundle in your hand. "You mean re-spool it? Yeah, I do, but..."
He looks at you oddly. "Alright," he says, putting the tapes back reluctantly.
He looks away. "You weren't quite yourself, officer."
He looks down. "Of course."

He looks off to the side, then down at his hands. "Can't say I'm a huge admirer of Wild Pines, and I certainly wouldn't trust any silver-tongued spokesperson of theirs. Fortunately, I have no reason to get involved."
He marvels at the cobalt shimmer, and nods: "Yes, these are very, very good. Did you defraud some foreign prince for them? Jump a Mesque banger? No matter... I'll give you 200 reál."
He nods reluctantly.
He nods to you reassuringly just as more diverse, higher-pitched sounds, some random, some appearing to form patterns, hit your eardrums.
He points at the white triangle on his orange safety jacket. "We were an all-volunteer force, self-organized. Tried to help fire brigades contain the spill."
He produces a machine encased in a blue bakelite shell, its black face covered in an assortment of pearl-topped knobs and dials.
He purses his lips. "Four reál is offensively low... but just this once. For the *musique concrète* cop."

He purses his lips. "I'm not sure. I wasn't even sure about our old recordings, which I no longer have... But I do have a tape with some ultrasonic sounds that *might* be what you're looking for. Would you like to hear?" He starts rummaging through some tapes behind the counter.
He scans the document in your hand. "This is--" He's interrupted by a sudden cough. "I certainly wouldn't pass up the opportunity to acquire something that can make princes out of peons."
He shakes his head slowly.
He shrugs. "I like theory more than story. Outward movement, not vortices."

He sighs. "Tiphaine Holly, the previous head of the Union, was rather *more* pleasant. Some of us around here... well, we've never understood why she didn't run for a second term. Or where she went after withdrawing from politics. It was all very strange."
He slowly finishes his thought: "...but I'm not some Mr. Fixit, I'm a pawnbroker. If you want to pawn the tape, sure. Although it looks pretty... worthless."
He smirks. "It's a simple matter of cause and effect, and recognizing that they work in both directions."
He steps back, away from the glass. "Oh, no, no, no, no. I don't need blood-thirsty mercenaries knocking on my door looking for their missing toys."
He studies the pin carefully, rolling it around in his palm. "Saint-Batiste Summer Dinghy Races '31. What a pleasant time *that* was."

He switches off the tape player. "You know, now that I've listened to it on these new speakers -- it's *not* the Col Do Ma Ma Daqua. Wrong patterns, wrong... photons. Probably some insect trying to sing higher than its predators can hear. Still -- fascinating, aren't they, early morning sounds?"
He takes a step back, studying you. "How would I know?"
He tenses. "I hadn't considered that... This is why I don't like to deal with guns."
He thinks about it. "I suppose that makes sense, yes. Please, go ahead and take it -- Welcome to Hjelmdall."
He thinks for a moment, then nods. "Sure, I can keep it behind the counter for a week -- but only if you pawn it right now."
He tilts his head. "I try to keep the shop at a comfortable temperature."
He watches you attach the sign to the street light using the sticky tack he put on the back of it. "There you go. Beautiful job."
His eyes move from you to the lights dancing on the walls.
His loosens up. "I'm not offended, officer."
Roy takes the hubcaps from the lieutenant and inspects them. The spinners appear iridescent in the dancing light of his pawnshop.
Suddenly, his gaze fixes on your tie. He steps back from the glass. "And *especially* that tie. It swallows photons around it. I have no need for *necrotic* objects."
The bric-à-brac man looks at you from behind two layers of polished glass. It is nearly impossible to read any emotion. He sways slightly and itches his cheek.
The light swirls in his face and glasses. He doesn't know what to say either.
The light swirls in his face and glasses. He doesn't know what to say.

The low range of sounds is easier to handle with a focal point, but still troubling. You are mesmerized by the sounds, but also feel nausea welling up as the motif continues, then begins to recede, dissolving in what must be the sound of water lapping at the bank...
The pawnbroker turns from you to the lieutenant and back again, a distant look on his face.
The pawnbroker's gaze is already fixed on the dancing colours.
The pawnshop owner uprights himself back into view with the stiffness of an old ironing board. "Here we go," he says, holding a piece of cardboard out at you.
You take some time to look around the store... The play of visuals all around the pawnshop is mesmerizing. Suddenly, Roy turns back to you with a reel of tape in his hand and coughs.
You tense up as the pawnshop owner uprights himself back into view. There isn't a gun in his hands -- or anywhere else on him. Instead, he holds out a piece of cardboard. "Here we go."
"...is the Harmon Wowshi W02 -- made in Vesper, designed in Seol," he says. "Plays all reel-to-reel formats: 2mm, 8mm, 12mm. It's even got a little radio in there. It'll set you back 12 reál."
"A *third*? Are you sure?"
"A Kristallsprach Model 9. Gottwaldian engineering at its finest. This is a specialist's model, ideal for picking up foreign signals..."

"A bad idea. Some poor leftists built a particle decay generator in hopes of bringing affordable electricity to under-served communities. It malfunctioned. Radioactive waste everywhere, probably some of it in *you*, too."
"A bunch of poor people built themselves a primitive nuclear reactor, hoping for the best. What do you think is going to happen?"
"A classic set. The figurines represent the Fifth-century Franconigerian Cavalry."
"A discount? I do have to keep the lights on, man. It's twelve reál."
"A fan... No, I wouldn't go that far. But I do think the Hjelmdallermann Saga is an integral part of our shared reality."
"A friend of mine knew of a way to deal with that. That's when I started riding the pyro, as they say. It helped -- a lot, actually. But it was another monthly outgoing... still is."
"A friend of mine knew of a way to deal with that. That's when I started riding the pyro, as they say. That did help -- a lot, actually. But it was another monthly outgoing... still is."
"A pin from '31 ought to be priced at 3.10 -- but I added another ten cents, just to be nice."
"A sanctuary filled with hand-picked positive photons... There would be no room for sadness in such a place. It's a brilliant vision..."
"A tape? We have boomboxes for sale that will play it. Check the shelves."
"A transceiver, is it? Yeah, we should have something to do the trick..."
"Absolutely. I've tested each one myself with recordings of speech, found sounds, and music from a variety of genres. Even though," he grimaces, "I don't really like music."
"Actually, yes. Let's. Eight is an even better number than twelve. Even more internal balance." He observes the light on the wall and adds: "Better integrity too."
"After I acquired the shop I had a bit of extra cash on my hands. Could do anything I wanted with it. So what *does* a young man do in that situation?"
"All kinds of people come through here... Locals, travellers. People looking for a deal. People looking for a keepsake. People who are terminally bored."
"Alright, alright. That'll have to do." His shoulders relax slightly. "The street light is all yours."
"Alright, you have a deal. The street light is all yours." His shoulders relax as if a load has been lifted off them. "Pleasure doing business with you."
"An *end* implies a stable state, whereas we can see from experience that everything is in fact always transforming. Thus, there can be no end."
"And I don't like keeping guns around the shop for long. Off-the-charts photon emissions. The unhealthy kind."
"And here you are. Quality sound reproduction on the go. It'll play anything. Wherever. Turn *any* tape into a conversation of sounds and shapes."
"And skuas. But shhhh." He raises a pointer finger and inclines his head toward the speakers. A new, high-pitched, shivering sound.
"Another time, perhaps."
"Anyhow, it's yours now..." He slides the tape closer to you on the counter top.
"Anything else you're thinking of selling?" Both the lieutenant and the pawnbroker turn to you.
"Anything else you're thinking of selling?"
"As I said, I refused to talk to him. That's why he came back a second time. That's *also* why he hasn't come back a third."
"As you can see... I have a wide selection of goods for everyone to choose from."
"Ask around the harbour. There might be some workers there who'd be willing to help."
"Besides, I've been to Katla, though not quite as far north as the Hjelmdall, and watched the northern lights travel across the sky. Very unique energetic tides there."
"Besides, this gear costs a fortune -- there's no one in Martinaise with that kind of money."
"Besides," he points to the sign on his booth, "there are no returns or exchanges for items purchased in this shop."
"Between you and me," he looks you up and down, "this is why I don't get involved in local politics."
"But I bowed out at some point. I prefer to watch from afar while the Big Wigs come and go."
"But I want to sell them *now*." He tilts his head slightly to consider this new information.
"But that's enough of my sob story. Let's get back to business," he says, as if this conversation has changed nothing between you.

"But the most important transformation is the light's placement among ordinary *indoor* fixtures, which has adjusted its morphological field. The light became suitable for use inside the home just a few days ago."
"But, yes, the books are very sexist. In a not-entirely-unenjoyable way."
"But... why? It's a perfectly wonderful light. Besides," he points to the sign on his booth, "there are no returns or exchanges for items purchased in this shop."
"But... why? It's a perfectly wonderful light."

"Cool or not... One of them was obsessed with recording the Col Do Ma Ma Daqua -- and he was one of those passionate people who know a lot about all kinds of strange things, so he got the rest of us to join in his search..."
"Could be, if you're not concerned about quality of signal. But real audiophiles will pay good money for this. That's why we can't let it go for less than 120 reál."
"Did I mention that this figurine is supposed to be lucky? Always carry it with you." He grins.
"Every day?" He tilts his head, studying you, then nods. "You look the part."
"Exactly. Cause and effect work in both directions."
"Excellent choice. I'm almost sad to part with it."
"Fifteen reál."
"Fifty cents. Bargain-priced! I'll throw in the tiny cap too -- I think he's looking for it, or something. That part of the story has many interpretations."
"Fine." He nods decisively. "Four reál it is."
"For a little while. Being cooped up alone most of the day wasn't healthy for me... just my own head to consort with. But a friend of mine knew of a way to deal with that."
"For a little while. But I soon started searching for other ways to cope with the mental trauma. Being cooped up alone most of the day was exacerbating it... just my own head to consort with."
"For sure. It's a consumer device with professional applications."
"For the moment, yes."
"Forget it, then. I'll get more for the light in cash. Unless you want to reconsider?"
"Greetings on this fine night. What brings you here?"
"Gulls and skuas. But shhhh." He raises a pointer finger and inclines his head toward the speakers. A new, very high-pitched, shivering sound emerges amidst the others.
"Had to take Pyrholidon for radiation sickness. That's what you were hinting at just now, wasn't it?"
"Have you tried it before?"
"He is a good one, that. Weather resistant."

"He left his native village of Hjelmdall after his son was kidnapped, having many exciting adventures and killing many enemies with his swords, but he lost his family in the process. Tragic stuff, really."
"He purchased a remarkably garish paperweight the first time he was here... Nothing the second."
"He tried. Wanted to come to some *mutually beneficial arrangement* around my dealings with the dockworkers... I politely declined to *hear him out*."
"He's been by the shop a couple of times." He gives a lazy half-shrug.
"Hell yeah, man." The shopkeep sounds enthusiastic. "I don't usually carry printed tees, but this one was just such a pure exemplar."
"Hello again. How can I help you?"
"Hello hello! Let me know if I can help you with anything."
"Here you go, man." He presents a large cap-shaped object on the palm of his hand. Very odd-looking...
"Here you go, officer." He hands you the pin. "Anything else I can do for you today?"
"Hey, I don't know where it came from, but it's not every day you get to buy and sell something so extraordinary..."
"Hm, that's a reasonable offer." He raises a curled finger to his chin, looking as thoughtful as he can.
"Hm?" He surfaces from a daydream. "Oh, right. That's... good," he replies, unsure of what you said.
"Hmm, I think you might be thinking about someone else I... dislike music," he frowns. "So I couldn't tell you who."
"How interesting! Well, it's been a while since I've gone hunting for the Col Do Ma Ma Daqua..."
"Huh?" He slowly taps his fingers on the counter. "What do you mean?"
"Huh?"
"I assure you it's not." He runs a finger along its edge. "See? Not a scratch. Now, please, take it and stick it on the street light. That way people will know it's *yours*."
"I deal in goods, not services."
"I do appreciate it."
"I do my best to keep my distance from all manner of butchery. Bad for business, bad for everyone."
"I don't like beaches. They accumulate too many photons, it's always chaos out there. But live your life, man. You can use it at a beach party if you want."
"I don't like either set very much, to be honest, but there are many parents among my customers."
"I doubt it, but I can try to answer any questions you may have."
"I felt within that thunderous crash a soul plunged into chaos."
"I haven't had any problems myself... though some of my customers have complained about inconsistent law enforcement."
"I just don't like it very much. Movement on the road never really gelled well with the movement of my thoughts."
"I lived by the river since I was a small boy. The Esperance... didn't have the heart to let it all go to shit without trying to *do* something, to help out."
"I mean -- even if the Man from Hjelmdall didn't exist before the adventure novels, the stories have made it so that he has. It's simple really."
"I rather like it *here* too, so yeah -- I'm not giving you my projector. This tape is all I can do for you and your friends' nightclub project." He nods at the fixed tape on the counter top.
"I respect your decision, officer. What else can I help you with?"
"I say: it's twelve reál. Four is a total ripoff. It's not even a number."
"I see you were wounded in the recent... altercation," he says with a grave nod. "A speedy recovery to you, officer."
"I see you were wounded in the recent... altercation." He nods gravely at your leg. "A speedy recovery to you, officer."
"I sure as hell didn't know. All I could think to do was pump it into the relief effort. I had to do *something* after I left the frontlines... for them, but also for myself."
"I sure as hell didn't know. So I pumped it into charities to help the less fortunate. I had to do something... for them, but also for myself."
"I sympathize, I do, but this is a for-profit enterprise."
"I think their poverty has been exaggerated for effect. When you place them next to the royalists, it doesn't seem like they could possibly win."
"I was with the Emergency Relief Brigade. Had to take it for radiation sickness."
"I wish I could help with that, officer, but I don't know where she was from or where she was going."
"I'd be glad to trade for your shares. Let's stick to that."
"I'm not purchasing any more clothing at the moment..." He looks you up and down quickly.
"I'm not purchasing any more clothing at the moment." He looks you up and down quickly. "And certainly not expensive armour that's liable to bring mercenaries to my doorstep."
"I'm sorry, there are no returns or exchanges for items purchased in this shop. Just enjoy it."
"I've *had* to take it, you know, since the People's Pile clean-up," he responds carefully. "I was with the Emergency Relief Brigade."
"If police work means playing tapes, sure. You can use it for that. Or any other time you'd need to play a tape."
"If you don't mind, please put the flashlight away. Some of us have photonic sensitivities."
"If you say so..."
"If you want to pawn... you're here..."
"In fact..." He leans in. "Most people don't think that the Man from Hjelmdall ever really existed, but they are *wrong*."
"In its purest form. Now, what can I do for you?"
"In theory, yes, you probably have enough to afford it all. However, I don't plan on selling up and joining the mastodons of La Delta just yet."
"Indeed." He immediately knows what you're talking about. "I think I even have his cap somewhere down here..." He looks for it. "A tiny miniature FALN cap to go with it. Yours for 50 cents."
"Interesting choice. But sure, why not -- take it. Welcome to Hjelmdall."
"Is it any good? The music, I mean."
"Is it?" He turns his head to the right and then to the left, as if looking for non-existent windows. "Spring is capricious, yes."
"It certainly does, especially in Revachol."
"It helped but it was another monthly outgoing... still is. It would have been fine but I was naive back then. Didn't think I'd ever run out of money..."
"It is quite heavy. You're going to need a truck."
"It keeps me entertained," he responds, unimpressed with your business-school snobbery.
"It keeps me entertained," he responds, unimpressed with your critique.
"It keeps me entertained," he responds, unimpressed with your snobbery.
"It keeps me entertained." His attention is drawn once more to the play of light and shadow on the walls behind you.
"It should belong to anyone who is ready to wear it."
"It was brought to me to be altered."
"It'll play that," the man nods. "Any Requiem really. Also dirges. Madrigals. Chants. As long as it's on tape."
"It's a logical explanation. I felt within that thunderous crash a soul plunged into chaos."
"It's a sign that declares you the owner of the street light. Stick it on and people will know that it's *yours*."
"It's about as close to perfection as a transceiver gets. And we're only asking 120 reál for it."
"It's no problem. Come back any time to look at it. It's *your* sawed off street light now."
"It's not often that I see officers from the RCM in my pawnshop." The man at the counter turns to you slowly.
"It's not that complicated. All that's required is a more robust understanding of cause and effect."
"It's simply a matter of recognizing that cause and effect work in both directions."
"Jacob Irw? The great TipTop champion? Yes, yes..."

"Keep in mind, I have to slow this one down enough to make sounds well over 200 kHz  audible to the human ear... It will be... strange." He switches on the tape player. The speakers begin to emit a low hum....
"Let me have a look."
"Let's just say there's some long overdue business I've got to deal with."
"Like... yeah."
"Man, you're really invested in this." He looks at the bundle of tape in front of him. It shimmers under the shop's dazzling light show.
"Maybe. Shady looking guys came in here yesterday, looking like they'd just taken off their Wild Pines overalls. They asked if I have a police weapon to sell. I told them I already sold it."
"Maybe."
"More than happy. I value the street light at 700 reál. You decide how many of your shares that gets me."
"More than happy. Like I said, I value the street light at 700 reál. You decide how many of your shares that gets me."
"More than sure. What else have you got?"
"Most people don't think that the Man from Hjemdall really existed, but they're *wrong*."
"My apologies, officer, but I have no idea where she was coming from or where she went."
"Neither is the Man a real man, of course, but both the Man and Hjelmdall are an ontological necessity..." He stops abruptly. "But, hey, it's not worth getting into an argument about."
"No apologies necessary, officer."
"No can do. I need to make money -- this is a business first and foremost. Not a charity."
"No chance. I've got a better grip on my finances these days. This is a mistake from my younger days that just won't go away."
"No offence but I don't think it would do me much good. Nothing to do with you -- it's just my customers tend to be, well... they wouldn't know who you are."
"No one's, everyone's..." He sighs and shakes his head.
"No, it's different... those film tapes actually *mean* something to me, but this is just a worthless bundle of old tape."
"No, just -- people like that make everyone else see the world somewhat askew... at an angle that is convenient for them. Now -- you have more questions, or are we..."
"No, not really. I expect momentous change at any moment... But it seems that *you* are." He almost sounds concerned and seems to weigh your offer.
"No... Being cooped up alone most of the day wasn't healthy for me -- just my own head to consort with. But a friend of mine knew of a way to deal with that."
"No... I soon started searching for other ways to cope with the mental trauma. Being cooped up alone most of the day was exacerbating it -- just my own head to consort with."
"Nothing else in here carries that much value, I'm afraid. Plus, I need to make sure I still earn *some* actual cash -- for food and such."
"Nothing's *wrong* with it. The shop suits me fine. It's just..." He changes tack. "We all need a bit of luck in our lives, you know? A lottery win."
"Now that I think about it, I do remember hearing a thunderous noise the other night -- some kind of powerful electric vortex hitting the shop and then moving on..."
"Now, what can I do for you?"
"Of course, officer." There's a tiny hint of distress in his voice. "It's your decision."
"Of course. I meant no offense. 200 reál for you, officer. Delightful doing business with you. Do come again."
"Of course. I'd be glad to trade for your shares. Let's stick to that."
"Of course. It's in working order still, isn't it? Just pick your tape and set it spinning. It all starts with the tape."
"Of course."
"Officer please, I'm serious."
"Officer, the flashlight please."
"Oh, I didn't mean to imply otherwise... Well, it's been a while since I've gone hunting for the Col Do Ma Ma Daqua myself..."
"Oh, it is."
"Oh, no, not at all." He flashes a smile. "I guess I haven't had many customers lately, RCM or otherwise."
"Oh, nothing like that." He is completely unfazed by your statement. "Just this sign that declares you the owner of the street light. Stick it on and people will know that it's *yours*."
"Oh, right. Perfect. Thank you."
"Oh, that's the Headless FALN Rider."
"Oh... I certainly hope not."
"Oh... I see. That's tough, man, I feel the same way sometimes. The Man from Hjelmdall is the hero of a series of popular books based on a fictional version of Katla."
"Oh... no, I don't like those kinds of objects. No sale." He barely even looks at it.
"Okay, I'll help you out. It's going to take a moment though, so just sit back and relax..."
"Okay." He doesn't bat an eye. "I don't like either set too much, to be honest."
"Once knew a group of young musicians who decided they didn't want to play music anymore and started looking for all kinds of interesting sounds instead..."
"Owning shares -- that's where the proper trade is. Far beyond the pittance I deal with in here."
"Perhaps." He shrugs. "I just like being awake for the transition between night and morning -- bearing witness to the first hints of light on the horizon."
"Radiowaves..."
"Right." He nods.
"Seven hundred reál. A bargain, I dare say."

"She didn't seem like a policeman, although she kept referring to herself as a *Pig*. Which was odd. I found her interest in the gun a bit... obsessive. But I was just happy to get rid of it. And of her."
"Sniffing is okay," says the shopkeep. "But please don't try anything on. Can't have you leaving your photon emissions in the fabric of things you're not going to buy."

"So I came to Martinaise. People told me don't go there, it's a *shit-hole*. I said: people, we just had a *nuclear pile meltdown*. I'm gonna get as far from Faubourg as I can. Still in the same city, but..." He shrugs.
"So it goes." The pawnbroker nods gravely, then shrugs. "Now, what can I do for you?" he asks.
"So much disappointment -- and early deaths, cancer mostly. And we knew all that was coming even as we were *cleaning up* as best we could."
"So, what do you want to know? Price? I can give you 3.20 for it."
"Someone else came here earlier today asking the same question -- I promptly sold her the gun you pawned a couple days back."
"Something like that, officer."
"Sorry, man. I can't be giving out freebies. Never have, won't now."
"Sounds like a ripoff, but okay. I can make it ten -- but no lower."
"Suit yourself. Can't promise this beauty'll be here when you come back, though." He gently returns the transceiver to its shelf behind the counter.
"Sure thing. So, do you want to sell anything?"
"Sure thing."
"Sure, man."
"Sure..." he mumbles as his eyes once again start following the light show around the pawnshop.
"Take a closer look. You'll see the quality of the craftsmanship then. Any other questions in the meantime?"
"Take your time."
"Tell you what..." He bends down and disappears behind the counter.
"That really wasn't the point. After the 'Simfonia' we moved onto the sounds of office supplies or something like that... and I doubt any of us would have been any good at pushing papers."
"That's alright, I can keep it here for you until you find one."

"That's fair. I just... It's been a long time since my Col Do Ma Ma Daqua hunting days," he responds with a thin smile. "Once knew a group of young musicians who decided they didn't want to play music anymore and started looking for all kinds of interesting sounds instead..."
"That's the Man from Hjelmdall walking away as his village burns."
"That's very sad, man. Then you missed out on some pretty well executed, albeit repetitive adventure literature."
"The Col Do Ma Ma Daqua?" He looks at you with astonishment. "Sorry, I would never have guessed that you were that interested in ultrasonic sounds... or *birds*, for that matter."

"The Headless FALN Rider. It's an urban legend -- about a man who rides the streets of Revachol sporting a FALN tracksuit. As you can see, he's missing his head." He points at the decapitated figurine.
"The Man from Hjelmdall is the hero of a series of popular books based on a fictional version of Katla, mostly what is nowadays Arda NFD."
"The Model 9 also comes equipped with a signal purifier to suppress crosstalk, especially good around here with our funky reception."
"The clean-up happened fifteen years ago. I was young then. Later my second aunt died, left me this shack and the assorted junk in it."
"The corpse behind the hostel, I assume..." He looks into the swirling lights, then to you: "I don't have a truck with a mounted platform or anything of that sort myself..."
"The dark always has its counterbalance in light. Neither will prevail. The cycle will continue." He folds his arms with finality and turns away from you, concentrating once more on his light show.
"The end... I don't know about that. Seemed more like a sign of a large-scale transformation. Shook the entire shack."
"The light has undergone three transformations, and every transformation, large or small, has a price tag." He rests his elbows on the counter and brings his face closer to the glass.
"The light... wow."

"The most important transformation is the light's placement among ordinary *indoor* fixtures, which has adjusted its morphological field. The light became suitable for use inside the home just a few days ago." He throws you a look of weary patience.
"The pawnshop is always open."
"The stuff I record myself -- silverware shaking in drawers as motorcars race by, nocturnal animals climbing on the roof, airship rotors, that kind of thing."
"There wasn't much the volunteer force could do, however. We wasted years in the river mud. Years getting sick..." He looks at the spiralling light and stops.

"There's also the matter of rewiring. But the most important transformation is the light's placement among ordinary *indoor* fixtures, which has adjusted its morphological field. The light became suitable for use inside the home just a few days ago."
